description: What every Atlas board package shares: the USB gadget's ids and network, the MAC rule, the identity endpoint and the gadget-net addressing. A package names it with "ecosystem" and inherits what its manifest leaves out (its own keys win). Records do not inherit. The board's own facts (its product name, hardware) stay in its manifest.

mac_rule.seed: board serial (lowercase hex, as in serial_source)
mac_rule.fallback_seed: "machine-id:" + /etc/machine-id when no serial is readable; with neither, no address is set and the kernel picks random ones. Never a fixed constant.
mac_rule.algorithm: base = 02:b0:b1:b2:b3:b4 where b0..b4 are the first 5 bytes of sha256(seed); host side = base with the last byte XOR 0x01; each interface XORs the last byte of both with its mask

usb_gadget.serial: board serial (first 16 hex digits of /etc/machine-id without one)

network.address: per board: capabilities.gadget-net.addressing (172.31.250.1/24 without a hex serial, or when USB_GADGET_ADDRESS pins one)
network.dhcp_range: the rest of the board's subnet after its address, at most 19 addresses (.2-.6 of a /29)
network.note: USB only: gadget interfaces are bridged with each other, never with Ethernet.

actions.notes: BOARD_ACTIONS in /etc/board/identity.env. A request drops /run/board/requests/<id>; a root path unit runs the action, so the endpoint stays unprivileged.

addressing.input: the gadget's USB serial (iSerialNumber, the board serial) normalized to Atlas's board-serial rule: all hex, at least 8 digits, the last 8 in lowercase
addressing.algorithm: h = the first 4 bytes of sha256(the 8 ASCII characters) as a big-endian u32; split base into /prefix subnets, drop those inside an exclude range, and take the remaining subnet at index h mod their count (8160), counting up from the lowest. The device has the subnet's first host address; DHCP offers the host the rest.
addressing.fallback: address (above), the fixed address of images before per-board addressing, when the serial gives no subnet or USB_GADGET_ADDRESS pins one; it is excluded from base so old and new boards never share a subnet
addressing.collisions: two boards on one computer share a subnet with probability 1/8160; among k boards about k(k-1)/16320 (0.55% for 10)
